transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. I came in because my mind just keeps going blank at the worst times. I work as a flagger, and... well, I'll look at the road-closure forms, or even just be holding the stop-slow paddle, and I suddenly can't remember the steps. It's like my brain just empties out. These are things I have done for years, and I suddenly just don't know what to do.
During these moments when your mind goes blank, do you also notice your heart pounding, sweating, trouble breathing, or a sense of intense fear or dread?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My heart doesn't race, and I'm not sweating or having trouble breathing. It's not really a scared feeling... it's just, well, empty. I'm not panicked, the thoughts are just gone.
During these episodes when your mind goes blank, do you ever lose consciousness or have moments where you're unaware of your surroundings, and afterward not remember what happened?

No, I don't pass out or anything like that. I know exactly where I am and what's going on around me. I'm still just standing there on the road... I just can't think. I remember everything that happens perfectly fine afterward, my brain just stops giving me the next step.
Did these blank-out episodes start after any particular frightening or traumatic event, like a close call or accident on the job?
No, there wasn't anything like that. I haven't been in any accidents or had any close calls on the job, or really anywhere else. It just started happening on its own.
During these blank spells, has anyone ever noticed you staring off, twitching, or making repetitive movements that you weren't aware of?

No, nobody has ever mentioned anything like that to me. I don't twitch or make any repetitive movements. I mean, I guess I might look like I'm staring just because I'm standing completely still, but... no, no one has ever told me I'm doing things I'm not aware of. I'm really just standing there holding my sign until my brain catches up.
Do these blank-out spells ever happen when you're relaxed and not under any pressure—like at home watching TV or just sitting quietly—or do they only occur while you're actively working?

No, it's really just when I'm working. When I'm at home, you know, watching TV or just sitting around, I don't have those moments where my mind just stops. It only seems to happen when I'm out there on the road with the sign.
Before or during your shifts, do you find yourself worrying a lot about making a mistake or not being able to remember the steps, even before your mind actually goes blank?

No, not really. I don't really worry about it beforehand. It's just... I'm just out there doing my job, and then suddenly it happens. I'm not sitting there stressing about making a mistake or forgetting what to do before the shift starts. It just hits me out of nowhere while I'm working.
During these episodes, do you ever feel detached from yourself or your surroundings—like you're watching yourself from outside, or like things around you feel unreal or dreamlike?

No, I don't think so. I don't feel like I'm outside my body or in a dream or anything like that. I'm just... there, but my mind goes blank. Everything around me still seems normal, it's just my brain that sort of pauses.
When your mind goes blank like this, about how long does each episode typically last before your thoughts come back?

It's hard to say exactly how long it lasts. It feels like a long time, but it's probably just a few minutes. But that's actually why I came in to see you. My mind just keeps going blank at the worst possible times. Like, I'll be looking at the road-closure forms, or I'll be holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just... I cannot remember the steps. And these are things I have done for years. It just completely leaves my head.
Aside from these specific episodes, do you feel any overall stress, tension, or unhappiness about your job or work environment right now?

No, not really. I mean, the job itself is fine. I've been doing it a long time. The people are okay, the environment is what it is. I'm not unhappy with the work itself or stressed out about the job in general. It's literally just this... this blanking out thing that's bothering me. Aside from that, work is just work.
During your shifts when this happens, are you often feeling very tired, sleep-deprived, or doing a long stretch of repetitive, monotonous standing before the blank spell occurs?

Well, the job is pretty much always a lot of standing and repetition. That's just what flagging is. But I wouldn't say I'm feeling sleep-deprived or extra tired when it happens. I get normal sleep. It just hits me randomly, even if I'm feeling fine and alert right before.
Do these blank-out episodes tend to happen at a particular time relative to your meals—like if you've skipped breakfast or gone a long stretch without eating during your shift?

I mean, I do skip meals a lot, but I haven't noticed if the blank spells happen right after. Honestly, food has just stopped meaning much to me lately. I'll go a long stretch and skip meals without even noticing it. I didn't really realize how much I wasn't eating until my flagger pants started feeling loose, and my family started asking why I look so drawn. But I don't know if that's what's causing the blanking out.
Aside from the eating changes, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy over the past few weeks?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's been pretty bad, actually. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness right in my chest. It just sits there. It honestly feels like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. I just feel so down, and I don't really care about much of anything anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way—the low mood, loss of interest, and appetite changes—has it been going on for at least two weeks?
It's been a lot longer than two weeks. The heavy depression, the guilt I've been feeling, having no energy, and losing my appetite... it's all been with me for about a year and two months now.

patient.answer: It's been a lot longer than two weeks. The heavy depression, the guilt I've been feeling, having no energy, and losing my appetite... it's all been with me for about a year and two months now.

inference.note: The prolonged (14-month) history of pervasive low mood, anhedonia, guilt, anergia, and significant unintentional weight loss indicates a major depressive episode of significant severity, which also explains the 'blanking out' spells as depression-related concentration/memory impairment. This effectively rules out dissociative causes, panic disorder, hypoglycemia (no clear meal-timing correlation, and symptoms don't fit hypoglycemic episodes), and elevates the depressive diagnosis from unspecified (F32.9) to a specific severe single-episode major depressive disorder (F32.2).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a pervasive, non-episodic depressive syndrome lasting over a year, marked by daily depressed mood, anhedonia, significant appetite/weight loss, guilt, and low energy—core and associated symptoms of a major depressive episode. Cognitive 'blank spells' are best explained as depression-related concentration/psychomotor disturbance rather than panic attacks, dissociation, seizures, or an anxiety disorder, given the absence of autonomic arousal, loss of awareness, dissociative features, or anticipatory worry. The chronicity, severity of vegetative symptoms (marked weight loss, guilt, anergia), and functional impact on work performance support a diagnosis of a single severe depressive episode without psychotic features.
